subject: Protempi: AZ1 sustained 5xx + latency — routing & exec brief
messages:
From: Lucy Perez <lucy.perez@protempi.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: support@protempi.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate and latency from AZ1 — immediate impact

Hi Vanessa,

We're seeing a sustained spike in 5xx errors and tail latency from requests routed to us-west-2a (AZ1) starting ~08:50 PT. Error rate is ~8% and median latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms; a few customers are reporting timeouts. This is impacting request flows for three of our production services (auth, search, recommendations).

We've opened a ticket with support (ID: PT-9192) but need to understand whether you have cross-region routing available today for our Dedicated pool or if we need a manual traffic diversion. Can you confirm scope and next steps? We're about to put a partial circuit breaker on client-side to reduce errors.

Attaching a small sample of error traces. Please escalate to engineering / oncall if this looks like platform-side.

Thanks,
Lucy
Product Ops — Protempi

Attachments: az1_error_sample_09021.txt (text)

Subject: Re: High error rate and latency from AZ1 — immediate impact

Thanks Lucy — I'm on this. I've looped in Rishi (oncall/infra), Ben (your CSM), and Grace (incident coordination). Rishi: can you validate whether this is a routing/capacity issue in AZ1 or an upstream model runtime failure? If routing, what are fast fallbacks we can apply (region drain, model variant fallback)?

Short plan: 1) confirm cause (Rishi) 2) if routing/capacity, trigger controlled cross-region drain to us-west-2b and us-west-2c for Protempi's Dedicated pool 3) notify customers & open exec channel if we need credits/SLA exceptions.

Lucy — we'll update in ~20 minutes with the initial diagnosis and a routing recommendation.

— Vanessa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency from AZ1 — immediate impact

Vanessa / team — quick diagnostic:
- Telemetry shows elevated token queueing and GPU-side KV cache pressure across the dedicated pool serving Protempi in AZ1 starting 08:47 PT.
- Model runtime logs show repeated transient OOM-ish fallbacks on a subset of pods; overall host-level resources are at ~92% GPU memory and pico-burst of CPU.
- No clear network partition; inter-AZ network RTTs are nominal.

Immediate mitigation I'm proposing (can execute in the next 10m):
1) Controlled drain: divert new traffic for Protempi from AZ1 -> AWs us-west-2b/2c using routing weight shift (gradual 30% -> 70% within 15m) to avoid cache storms.
2) Autoscaling bump for Protempi's Dedicated pool (add 2 medium GPU nodes) to absorb burst and reduce queuing.
3) Apply model-variant fallback for the heaviest endpoints (ranker) to a slightly quantized model with same semantics for 15m window.

Risks: cache misses during reroute may spike tail latency briefly; we should throttle rate for heavy clients during the shift.

I'll start the weight shift and autoscaling now. Will post live metrics.

— Rishi (Infra oncall)
From: Lucy Perez <lucy.perez@protempi.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency from AZ1 — immediate impact

Thanks for the quick response. We're starting to see some relief on auth but search is still noisy. A few notes from our side:
- Peak traffic is user search during morning ramp — if you throttle, please keep the weight shift smooth.
- We may need a formal credit request if this impacts SLOs beyond 30 minutes (we have a committed SLA).

If this looks like a capacity-only event and you expect full recovery within ~30-45 minutes, we can hold off on an exec call. Otherwise our VP of Engineering is standing by to join.

— Lucy
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: CEO <ceo@redwood.com>, VP Product <vp_product@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief: Protempi AZ1 surge — request for rapid credit approval & channel support

Team — quick executive summary and ask (for distribution to company leadership):
- Impact: Protempi (Dedicated customer, high ARR) observed sustained 5xxs (~8%) and tail latency from AZ1 starting 08:47 PT; primary affected endpoints: auth, search, ranker.
- Initial action (completed by infra): controlled routing weight shift from AZ1 -> us-west-2b/2c; autoscaling + variant fallback applied. Early telemetry: 5xxs down to ~2.1%, median latency trending back toward 200–250ms.
- Customer posture: Lucy Perez requests a credit if SLOs are missed beyond 30 mins; VP Eng may join if not contained.

Requesting: 1) pre-approve up to a $12k credit for Protempi if the incident extends beyond 45 minutes; 2) Sales/CS to join the customer bridge and own customer comms (Ben/Grace); 3) Exec-level standby for an optional sync if recovery stalls.

I'll keep you posted with a final incident rundown and the planned RCA.

— Vanessa
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lucy Perez <lucy.perez@protempi.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and latency from AZ1 — immediate impact

Update summary for the thread (closing loop):
- Routing: weight shift completed steadily over 18 minutes; traffic now ~85% diverted from AZ1 to us-west-2b/2c for Protempi.
- Autoscale: +2 GPU nodes added and are healthy.
- Metrics: 5xxs stabilized at 0.6%, median latency ~170ms, p95 back to ~420ms — still above baseline but acceptable.
- Customer comms: Ben & I did a 1:1 with Lucy at 12:30 PT; they requested the $12k credit pre-approval; finance liaison assigned PR-logs for post-incident credit review.

Attachments: routing_plan_protempi_az1.pdf (PDF) — contains the exact weight schedule and rollback criteria.

Next steps: RCA (ops) + model runtime investigation (infra) to be delivered within 72 hours. Closing incident channel but keeping an active watch for 6 hours.

— Grace
